text:
Maya C: heads up — after the latest redwoodctl release on Windows I started seeing auth failures in local testing.

Maya C: steps to repro:
1) install using winget
2) create profile `localtest`
3) run `redwoodctl auth login --profile localtest`

Maya C: CLI prints "failed to start auth flow: exec: \"redwoodctl.exe\": file does not exist" even though `redwoodctl --version` works

Devon: do you have multiple redwoodctl binaries on PATH? `where redwoodctl` or `Get-Command redwoodctl` helps

Maya C: output from PowerShell:
```
PS> Get-Command redwoodctl
CommandType     Name                                               Version    Source
-----------     ----                                               -------    ------
Application     redwoodctl.exe                                     0.0.0      C:\Users\maya\scoop\shims\redwoodctl.exe
Application     redwoodctl.exe                                     0.0.0      C:\Program Files\Redwood\bin\redwoodctl.exe
```

Maya C: seems the shim points to a non-executable because scoop's shim forwards to a path that no longer exists after the winget install. Auth flow runs `redwoodctl auth open-browser` which shells out to the shim, and the shim fails.

Samir: ahh path race — shim -> missing target. Workaround: remove the old shim or reorder PATH so Program Files comes first. Also `redwoodctl auth login --browser none` to get device code

Maya C: try `where.exe`:
```
C:\Users\maya\scoop\shims\redwoodctl.exe
C:\Program Files\Redwood\bin\redwoodctl.exe
```

Maya C: CI Bot: this is why our localtest pipeline failed on Windows runners

CI Bot: noticed failing job test/local-windows after 3:45pm PST, error lines include "exec: \"redwoodctl.exe\": file does not exist"

Devon: we should add a post-install check that validates shims and warns about multiple installations. Maybe `redwoodctl doctor --fix-shims`?

Samir: short-term, update the installer to remove legacy shims on upgrade. Long-term: make auth flow use full path resolution instead of relying on shell to pick the first executable (race when shim points to dead target)

Ashley: can you paste your %PATH% and the contents of the shim file? scoop shims are small .ps1 wrappers sometimes

Maya C: shim content (scoop shim exe wrapper):
```
@echo off
"C:\Users\maya\scoop\apps\redwoodctl\current\redwoodctl.exe" %*
```

Maya C: quickly fixed by deleting C:\Users\maya\scoop\shims\redwoodctl.exe and re-running auth, worked :thumbsup:

Devon: filed issue #3421 to track installer/shim interactions and added reproduction steps. tagging @eng-runtime @devex

ops-bot: incident created: PROD-WINDOWS-SHIM-3421

Maya C: leaving note — also affected local config profile token cache path. the race caused partial token file to be left at `%USERPROFILE%\.redwood\token.lock` which blocked subsequent logins until deleted

Samir: noted, will add token lock cleanup on failed auth

Ashley: thanks for the clear repro and logs, good catch :eyes:
